questions.question_text: Book-keeping is the art of:
options: Recording business transactions systematically in books of account
questions.explanation: It is the recording base of accounting.

questions.question_text: R.N. Carter defined book-keeping as the science and art of correctly recording in books of account all those business transactions that result in:
options: The transfer of money or money's worth
questions.explanation: Transfer of money or money's worth is the key idea.

questions.question_text: An objective of book-keeping is:
options: To maintain systematic and permanent records of transactions
questions.explanation: It also helps in finding profit and the financial position.

questions.question_text: A feature of book-keeping is that it:
options: Records only financial transactions in chronological order
questions.explanation: It is a clerical process.

questions.question_text: The two systems of book-keeping are:
questions.explanation: Double entry is the complete system.

questions.question_text: The double entry principle states that:
options: Every debit has an equal and corresponding credit
questions.explanation: Both aspects of each transaction are recorded.

questions.question_text: In accounting, debit and credit are:
options: The left side (Dr) and the right side (Cr) of an account
questions.explanation: They are positions, not necessarily increase or decrease.

questions.question_text: A debit entry:
options: Does not always mean an increase; it increases assets and expenses but decreases liabilities and capital
questions.explanation: The effect depends on the type of account.

questions.question_text: The Italian system of book-keeping is another name for:
questions.explanation: Luca Pacioli described it in 1494.

questions.question_text: The Cameral system is used for:
questions.explanation: It was developed for government accounting in Europe.

questions.question_text: The three types of accounts are:
questions.explanation: Based on the English approach.

questions.question_text: Personal accounts are classified into:
questions.explanation: They relate to persons.

questions.question_text: A natural person's account (e.g., Ram's A/c) is a:
questions.explanation: Artificial persons include firms and companies.

questions.question_text: Representative personal accounts are accounts that:
options: Represent persons, e.g., outstanding rent and prepaid insurance
questions.explanation: They represent persons to whom money is owed or from whom it is due.

questions.question_text: Real accounts relate to:
options: Assets and properties, e.g., cash, building
questions.explanation: They can be tangible or intangible.

questions.question_text: Goodwill is a:
questions.explanation: Tangible assets can be touched, e.g., furniture.

questions.question_text: Nominal accounts relate to:
questions.explanation: E.g., rent, salary, commission received.

questions.question_text: Nominal accounts are called fictitious because:
options: They have no physical existence and are closed at year end
questions.explanation: They are transferred to the profit and loss account.

questions.question_text: The golden rule for personal accounts is:
options: Debit the giver, credit the receiver
Debit the receiver, credit the giver
Debit what comes in, credit what goes out
Debit expenses and losses, credit incomes and gains
questions.explanation: The receiver of the benefit is debited.

questions.question_text: The golden rule for real accounts is:
options: Debit what comes in, credit what goes out
Debit the receiver, credit the giver
questions.explanation: Assets coming in are debited.

questions.question_text: The golden rule for nominal accounts is:
options: Debit what comes in, credit what goes out
Debit the receiver, credit the giver
Debit all expenses and losses, credit all incomes and gains
questions.explanation: Expenses and losses are debited.

questions.question_text: Under the American (accounting equation) approach, assets and expenses are _____ when they increase:
questions.explanation: Liabilities, capital and incomes are credited when they increase.

questions.question_text: An increase in assets is recorded by:
questions.explanation: Assets have debit balances.

questions.question_text: An increase in liabilities is recorded by:
questions.explanation: Liabilities have credit balances.

questions.question_text: An increase in capital is recorded by:
questions.explanation: Capital has a credit balance.

questions.question_text: An increase in expenses is recorded by:
questions.explanation: Expenses have debit balances.

questions.question_text: An increase in income is recorded by:
questions.explanation: Incomes have credit balances.

questions.question_text: A decrease in assets is recorded by:
questions.explanation: The opposite side from the increase.

questions.question_text: A decrease in liabilities is recorded by:
questions.explanation: The opposite side from the increase.

questions.question_text: Drawings are recorded by:
options: Debiting capital in the ledger always
questions.explanation: Drawings account is debited and closed to capital.

questions.question_text: The English system differs from the American system in that the English system uses:
options: Personal, real and nominal accounts and golden rules
questions.explanation: The American system uses the accounting equation.

questions.question_text: Both systems give the same result because:
options: Each transaction affects debit and credit equally under either approach
questions.explanation: They are two ways of reaching the same entry.

questions.question_text: Commenced business with cash: Cash A/c is _____, Capital A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Cash is real (comes in); capital is personal (giver).

questions.question_text: Purchased furniture for cash: Furniture A/c is _____, Cash A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Furniture comes in; cash goes out.

questions.question_text: Purchased goods on credit from Ram: Purchases A/c is _____, Ram's A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Goods (expense of trade) come in; Ram is the giver.

questions.question_text: Sold goods on credit to Shyam: Shyam's A/c is _____, Sales A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Shyam is the receiver; sales is income.

questions.question_text: Paid rent in cash: Rent A/c is _____, Cash A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Rent is an expense; cash goes out.

questions.question_text: Received commission: Cash A/c is _____, Commission Received A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Commission received is income.

questions.question_text: Withdrew cash for personal use: Drawings A/c is _____, Cash A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Drawings reduce capital.

questions.question_text: Paid outstanding wages: Outstanding Wages A/c is _____, Cash A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: The liability is cleared.

questions.question_text: Received interest from the bank: Bank A/c is _____, Interest Received A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Interest received is income.

questions.question_text: Depreciation on machinery: Depreciation A/c is _____, Machinery A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Depreciation is an expense that reduces the asset.

questions.question_text: Bad debts written off: Bad Debts A/c is _____, Debtor's A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Bad debts is a loss.

questions.question_text: Discount allowed to a customer: Discount Allowed A/c is _____, Customer's A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Discount allowed is a loss.

questions.question_text: Discount received from a supplier: Supplier's A/c is _____, Discount Received A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Discount received is a gain.

questions.question_text: Goods returned to the supplier: Supplier's A/c is _____, Purchases Returns A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: The supplier is the receiver of goods.

questions.question_text: Goods returned by a customer: Sales Returns A/c is _____, Customer's A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: The customer is the giver of goods.

questions.question_text: Paid insurance premium in advance: Prepaid Insurance A/c is _____, Cash A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Prepaid insurance is an asset.

questions.question_text: Received cash from the debtor: Cash A/c is _____, Debtor's A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Debtor is the giver.

questions.question_text: Paid salary by cheque: Salary A/c is _____, Bank A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Salary is an expense.

questions.question_text: Bought a machine on credit: Machinery A/c is _____, Supplier's A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Machine comes in; supplier is the giver.

questions.question_text: Deposited cash into the bank: Bank A/c is _____, Cash A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Bank balance increases.

questions.question_text: Withdrew cash from the bank for office use: Cash A/c is _____, Bank A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Cash comes in; bank goes out.

questions.question_text: Owner introduced additional capital in cash: Cash A/c is _____, Capital A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Capital increases.

questions.question_text: Goods lost by fire: Loss by Fire A/c is _____, Purchases (Stock) A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Loss is debited; goods go out.

questions.question_text: Goods distributed as free samples: Advertisement A/c is _____, Purchases A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: It is an advertising expense.

questions.question_text: Interest charged on drawings: Drawings A/c is _____, Interest on Drawings A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Interest on drawings is an income of the business.

questions.question_text: Interest allowed on capital: Interest on Capital A/c is _____, Capital A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Interest on capital is an expense.

questions.question_text: Rent received in advance: Cash A/c is _____, Rent Received in Advance A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: It is a liability to the business.

questions.question_text: Loan taken from a bank: Cash/Bank A/c is _____, Loan A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Cash comes in; the bank is the giver.

questions.question_text: Paid interest on the loan: Interest A/c is _____, Cash A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Interest paid is an expense.

questions.question_text: Sold old furniture for cash: Cash A/c is _____, Furniture A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Cash comes in; furniture goes out.

questions.question_text: Goods taken by the owner for personal use: Drawings A/c is _____, Purchases A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: It is a drawing.

questions.question_text: Cash stolen: Loss by Theft A/c is _____, Cash A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Theft is a loss.

questions.question_text: Sold goods for cash: Cash A/c is _____, Sales A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Sales is income.

questions.question_text: Purchased goods for cash: Purchases A/c is _____, Cash A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Purchases come in.

questions.question_text: Paid commission to an agent: Commission A/c is _____, Cash A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Commission paid is an expense.

questions.question_text: Received dividend: Cash A/c is _____, Dividend Received A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Dividend is income.

questions.question_text: Accrued income: Accrued Income A/c is _____, Income A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: Accrued income is an asset.

questions.question_text: Provision for doubtful debts created: Profit and Loss A/c (Bad Debts) is _____, Provision for Doubtful Debts A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: The provision is a charge against profit.

questions.question_text: Bad debts recovered: Cash A/c is _____, Bad Debts Recovered A/c is _____:
questions.explanation: It is a gain.

questions.question_text: A debit note is issued by:
options: The buyer to the seller for goods returned or for a correction
questions.explanation: The buyer debits the seller's account.

questions.question_text: A credit note is issued by:
options: The seller to the buyer for goods returned or overcharge
questions.explanation: The seller credits the buyer's account.

questions.question_text: Which is NOT a source document?
questions.explanation: The trial balance is a statement from the ledger.

questions.question_text: A cash memo is:
options: A document prepared for a cash sale
questions.explanation: It is the evidence of a cash transaction.

questions.question_text: An invoice differs from a bill in that an invoice is:
options: A document listing goods sold with quantity, price and terms
questions.explanation: Often used interchangeably, an invoice is for goods, a bill for services.

questions.question_text: A pay-in-slip is used for:
options: Depositing cash or cheques in the bank
questions.explanation: The bank gives a receipt.

questions.question_text: Vouchers in book-keeping:
questions.explanation: They support entries for audit.

questions.question_text: The capital account is a personal account because:
options: It represents the owner, to whom the business owes the capital
questions.explanation: The business is a separate entity.

questions.question_text: The drawings account is a personal account because:
questions.explanation: It is a part of the proprietor's capital.

questions.question_text: Goodwill is a real account because:
questions.explanation: It has value but no physical form.

questions.question_text: A debit note differs from a credit note in that the debit note is issued by the:
options: Buyer; credit note by the seller
Seller; credit note by the buyer
Bank; credit note by the government
questions.explanation: Both adjust the other party's account.

questions.question_text: Capital increases are credited because:
options: Assets = Liabilities + Capital, and the credit side represents capital
questions.explanation: Capital is on the right side of the equation.

questions.question_text: Assets are shown on the:
questions.explanation: Assets have debit balances.

questions.question_text: Liabilities are shown on the:
questions.explanation: Liabilities have credit balances.

questions.question_text: The sum of debits equals the sum of credits because:
options: Every transaction has equal debit and credit aspects
questions.explanation: Double entry ensures this.

questions.question_text: Bought goods on credit and sold on credit: the accounts affected are:
questions.explanation: Two entries: purchase and sale.

questions.question_text: Examples of real, personal and nominal accounts respectively are:
questions.explanation: Real: cash; personal: Ram; nominal: rent.

questions.question_text: If only assets are involved in a transaction, the total of assets:
questions.explanation: One asset increases and another decreases.

questions.question_text: Paying a creditor:
questions.explanation: Cash and creditors both fall.

questions.question_text: An outstanding expense account shows:
options: An expense incurred but not yet paid (a liability)
questions.explanation: E.g., outstanding rent.

questions.question_text: A prepaid expense account shows:
options: An expense paid in advance for a future period (an asset)
questions.explanation: E.g., prepaid insurance.

questions.question_text: An accrued income account shows:
options: Income earned but not yet received (an asset)
questions.explanation: E.g., interest receivable.

questions.question_text: Income received in advance is:
options: A liability (income of a future period)
questions.explanation: It will be earned later.

questions.question_text: Cash discount is a nominal account because it:
options: Represents a loss or gain (an expense or income)
questions.explanation: Discount allowed is a loss; discount received is a gain.

questions.question_text: Trade discount is not recorded in the books because:
options: It is deducted from the list price on the invoice and only the net amount is recorded
questions.explanation: Only the net price enters the books.

questions.question_text: "Debit the receiver, credit the giver" applies to:
questions.explanation: Real and nominal accounts have their own rules.

questions.question_text: An account can have a debit balance and a credit balance at the same time:
options: No; the net balance is either debit or credit
questions.explanation: The balance is the difference between the two sides.

questions.question_text: A debit entry on an expense account:
questions.explanation: Expenses have debit balances.

questions.question_text: A credit entry on a liability account:
questions.explanation: Liabilities have credit balances.
